title: Integral character line and twisted sections of a finite etale torsor
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention], and let $Q,W$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ with their small etale sites [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $G$ be a finite group and let $q:W\to Q$ be a representable surjective etale morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism] with a left $G$-action over $Q$ for which $(g,w)\mapsto(gw,w)$ identifies $\coprod_{g\in G}W$ with $W\times_QW$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Let $\chi:G\to\{1,-1\}\subset\mathbf Z^\times$ be a group homomorphism. Here $\underline{\mathbf Z}$ is the constant integer sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Define $q_*$ on abelian etale sheaves by sections over $W\times_QV$ for etale objects $V\to Q$, and define $$L_\chi=(q_*\underline{\mathbf Z})^\chi=\{t:\ g^*t=\chi(g)t\ \forall g\in G\}.$$ Then $L_\chi$ is etale locally isomorphic to $\underline{\mathbf Z}$, and $q^{-1}L_\chi\cong\underline{\mathbf Z}$. Over a trivialization $W\times_QV\cong\coprod_{g\in G}V$ it is generated by $v_\chi=\sum_g\chi(g)e_g$ in $\mathbf Z[G]$. There is a canonical isomorphism $L_\chi\otimes_{\mathbf Z}L_\chi\cong\underline{\mathbf Z}$, locally $v_\chi\otimes v_\chi\mapsto1$. For every abelian sheaf $F$ on $Q_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] the canonical tensor-section map induces natural isomorphisms $$(q_*q^{-1}F)^\chi\cong F\otimes_{\mathbf Z}L_\chi,\qquad \Gamma(W,q^{-1}F)^\chi\cong\Gamma(Q,F\otimes_{\mathbf Z}L_\chi).$$ Tensor means the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The isomorphisms hold for arbitrary abelian sheaves, including ones with torsion dividing $|G|$, and commute with all maps of such sheaves.

source.place: Tag 0727, lemma-twist, statement and proof; the self-dual tensor pairing is the transition-character consequence of the local generator in that proof.

proof.text: Work on the small scheme-chart site of $Q$. For every object $T\to Q$, $W_T=W\times_QT$ is a scheme and $W_T\to T$ is a surjective etale cover by the representability assumption and [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Composing it with $T\to Q$ gives another object of the site by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. The projection $W_T\to W$ is a section of the pulled-back torsor over $W_T$, so the assumed torsor isomorphism gives a $G$-equivariant trivialization there, with component $g$ given by $g$ times that section. Thus the family of scheme objects admitting a lift to $W$ covers every object of $Q_{\mathrm{et}}$. It is small in [def-weil-size-convention]. This uses no assertion that the possibly nonschematic space $W$ itself is an object of the scheme-chart site.

source.place: Tag 0727 (lemma-twist), proof, first three sentences: trivialize the torsor by itself, implemented on scheme charts

proof.text: The eigensections form a sheaf: compatible sections in the ambient sheaf glue uniquely, and each equation $g^*t=\chi(g)t$ holds for the glued section because it holds on a cover [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. On a trivializing object $V$ and every object $T\to V$, the sheaf axiom for the disjoint components of $W_T=\coprod_{h\in G}T$ identifies $q_*q^{-1}F(T)$ with $\prod_h F(T)$. Here etale inverse image is restriction on the localized sites [def-trf-algebraic-space], so the component at $h$ is precisely $F(T)$ with its original restriction maps. Similarly $q_*\underline{\mathbf Z}|_V$ is the product of copies of the restricted constant integer sheaf. Constant sheaves restrict to the same constant sheaf by [lem-weil-pbc-site-constant-restriction]. Empty components have the zero group by the empty-cover sheaf axiom. All these identifications commute with restriction and with maps of $F$.

source.place: Tag 0727 (lemma-twist), proof, displayed regular-representation description and the following restriction to the trivializing cover

proof.text: Write a section in the product as $(a_h)_{h\in G}$. Pullback by $g$ takes its $h$-coordinate to $a_{gh}$, so its character equation is $a_{gh}=\chi(g)a_h$. Setting $h=1$ gives $a_g=\chi(g)a_1$; conversely this formula satisfies every equation since $\chi(gh)=\chi(g)\chi(h)$. Therefore evaluation at $1$ and $a\mapsto(\chi(h)a)_h$ are inverse homomorphisms for every abelian group of sections, with no divisibility hypothesis. Apply this first to the constant integer sheaf: on $V$, $L_\chi$ is freely generated by $v_\chi=(\chi(h))_h=\sum_h\chi(h)e_h$. The local generator map and its inverse commute with restrictions, giving the claimed local isomorphism of sheaves.

source.place: Tag 0727 (lemma-twist), proof, local generator and the sentence describing semi-invariants of $M[G]$

proof.text: There is also a specified trivialization after pullback to $W$. On every etale scheme chart $T\to W$, the tautological lift $T\to W$ gives the preceding trivialization of $W\times_QT$; send a restricted eigensection to its value on this lift. For every further etale chart map these evaluation maps commute with restriction. The inverse sends an integer section $a$ to the tuple $(\chi(g)a)_g$ relative to that lift, so the two composites are the identity by step 3. Etale inverse image is restriction [def-trf-algebraic-space], and [lem-weil-pbc-site-constant-restriction] identifies its constant target on each chart. These chartwise maps define $q^{-1}L_\chi\cong\underline{\mathbf Z}$ on $W_{\mathrm{et}}$.

source.place: Tag 0727 (lemma-twist), proof, the choice of a lift determining the regular-representation coordinates

proof.text: For an etale scheme $T\to Q$ and $s,t\in L_\chi(T)$, multiply their integer-valued sections on $W_T$. The product is invariant because $g^*(st)=\chi(g)^2st=st$. On $W_T\times_TW_T=\coprod_gW_T$, its two restrictions consequently agree. The sheaf equalizer axiom [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] descends it uniquely to an integer section $b_T(s,t)$ on $T$. Restrictions, addition, and integer scalar multiplication commute with this descent by uniqueness, so $b$ is a bilinear map of sheaves, defined without a choice of lift. The sheafified-tensor definition [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and the universal property in [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] give a canonical morphism $b:L_\chi\otimes_{\mathbf Z}L_\chi\to\underline{\mathbf Z}$. On a trivializing chart $s=av_\chi,t=cv_\chi$ have product the constant tuple $(ac)_g$, hence $b(av_\chi\otimes cv_\chi)=ac$.

source.place: Tag 0727 (lemma-twist), proof, local generator; canonical self-dual pairing obtained by descending the product of two character sections

proof.text: Localize to a trivializing scheme object $V$. Tensor sheafification commutes with this restriction by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheafification-restriction]: the forgetful functor from the slice site is continuous and cocontinuous, since covers are precisely covers of the underlying domains and every cover of a domain lifts over its fixed map to $V$. Thus the tensor can be computed from the two restricted factors. The formula in step 5 has the inverse $a\mapsto a(v_\chi\otimes v_\chi)$: on pure tensors the two composites are the identity, and the universal property of sheafification extends this identity to the tensor sheaf. Apply [lem-sfb-sheaf-cover-local-isomorphism] to the covering family of step 1, with $\mathcal A=\mathrm{Ab}$, to conclude that $b$ is an isomorphism globally. This also gives the stated normalization $v_\chi\otimes v_\chi\mapsto1$.

source.place: Tag 0727 (lemma-twist), proof, local rank-one computation, with the tensor-square normalization checked on the trivializing cover

proof.text: For arbitrary $F$, on each object $T\to Q$ the formula $a\otimes t\mapsto (a|_{W_T})t$ defines a morphism from the presheaf tensor into $q_*q^{-1}F$; multiplication here is the ordinary integer action on the restricted abelian sheaf. Its value satisfies the character equations because the pullback of $a$ is invariant and $t$ is a character section. By [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] it extends uniquely to $\alpha_F:F\otimes_{\mathbf Z}L_\chi\to(q_*q^{-1}F)^\chi$. On a trivializing chart it is $a\otimes nv_\chi\mapsto(\chi(g)na)_g$. By step 3 its inverse is evaluation at $1$ followed by $a\mapsto a\otimes v_\chi$. The two composites are identities on pure tensors and on all eigentuples; module-sheafification restriction [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheafification-restriction] makes these computations valid on the localized tensor sheaf. The covering family of step 1 and [lem-sfb-sheaf-cover-local-isomorphism] imply that $\alpha_F$ is an isomorphism globally. Take its inverse for the orientation in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0727 (lemma-twist), proof, tensor-section identification and the calculation of semi-invariants of $M[G]$

proof.text: For a map $u:F\to F'$, the equation $u((a|_{W_T})t)=(u(a)|_{W_T})t$ holds on each pure tensor. The sheafification universal property [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] therefore proves naturality of $\alpha_F$ and of its inverse. Finally a global section of the eigensubsheaf is exactly a global section of $q_*q^{-1}F$ satisfying every character equation: both conditions are imposed on compatible sections over all scheme charts. By the definition of $q_*$ these compatible sections are $\Gamma(W,q^{-1}F)$. Hence applying $\Gamma(Q,-)$ to step 7 gives $\Gamma(W,q^{-1}F)^\chi\cong\Gamma(Q,F\otimes_{\mathbf Z}L_\chi)$. No exactness of the semi-invariant functor or averaging idempotent was used. The same formulas apply when $G$ is trivial, when $Q$ is empty, and when $F$ has torsion dividing $|G|$.

source.place: Tag 0727 (lemma-twist), proof, final sentence: take global sections; coefficient naturality checked on the tensor-section formula

tool_uses.why: Base change of the torsor cover gives an actual scheme cover of each scheme-chart object; generic algebraic-space cover calculus.
Composition keeps the trivializing scheme charts etale over Q; generic representability and etale permanence.
Restriction to a slice commutes with module sheafification, needed to compute the actual sheaf tensor on a trivializing cover. No node of this unit supplies this generic site fact.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NH-f9dee18c1 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS, no changes. I read all eight steps and every cited statement, plus Stacks 0727 (lemma-twist), spaces-cohomology.tex lines 928-992. The statement keeps every clause of the base and only adds the [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] reference; nothing is weakened. The item is still unsplit in both live clones, so it is not superseded. There are no new nodes, and searching dag/nodes for 0727, character line and semi-invariant found no duplicate. The steps follow the Stacks route: base change gives a scheme cover with a trivialization (fibre-products and representable-tests lemmas); the eigensheaf is a sheaf and is a product on trivializing charts (constant-restriction lemma applies to any small site); the coordinate calculation a_g=chi(g)a_1 holds for every abelian group; q^{-1}L≅Z comes from the tautological lift; the pairing is the descended pointwise product, using chi^2=1 and the equalizer axiom; it and alpha_F are isomorphisms by restricting to the slice (module-sheafification-restriction lemma) and checking on the cover; naturality and global sections finish the proof. I checked both composites of alpha_F by hand. Edge cases checked: G trivial, chi trivial, C2 with F=Z/2 and Z/4 (no averaging needed), nonabelian G, Q empty. Batch-5 flag: lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests is generic algebraic-space foundations (Stacks 03EC/025W). Its 144-node closure contains no trace-formula or Poincaré-duality node, so it lies outside the assumed statements. The tool_uses for the two trf lemmas and lem-weil-pbc-module-sheafification-restriction are generic and accepted.
